en.name: Ideal body weight
en.shortDescription: Ideal body weight (IBW) — a height-based target weight used for dosing and ventilator settings; in kilograms (kg).
en.longDescription:
## Definition & Clinical Context

Ideal body weight (IBW) is a *calculated* target weight derived from a patient's height and sex, not a measured weight. It produces a single numeric value used to set drug doses and tidal-volume ventilator settings independently of the patient's actual (possibly oedematous or obese) weight. It is reported in kilograms (kg).

## Included Concepts

- *4062985 / 170804003 — Ideal body weight (SNOMED)* and *3032445 / 50064-5 — Ideal body weight (LOINC)*: the standard height/sex-based target weight. The two concepts are equivalent, both standard and in the Measurement domain; either one is correct.

## Mapping Notes

- Map a calculated target weight here — **not** a measured weight (measured weight belongs in the *Body weight* set).
- **Adjusted ideal body weight is a different quantity**: *1073500 / 1304200008 — Adjusted ideal body weight (SNOMED)* is derived from IBW and the actual body weight (corrected for obesity). It has the same unit but differs from IBW whenever the actual weight does, markedly in obese patients, so it is not part of this set: mixing it in would bias a tidal volume expressed per kg of IBW.

fr.longDescription:
## Définition et contexte clinique

Le poids corporel idéal (IBW) est un poids cible *calculé* à partir de la taille et du sexe du patient, et non un poids mesuré. Il produit une valeur numérique unique servant à régler les posologies et le volume courant ventilatoire indépendamment du poids réel (parfois œdémateux ou obèse). Il est exprimé en kilogrammes (kg).

## Concepts inclus

- *4062985 / 170804003 — Ideal body weight (SNOMED)* et *3032445 / 50064-5 — Ideal body weight (LOINC)* : le poids cible standard fondé sur la taille et le sexe. Les deux concepts sont équivalents, tous deux standard et du domaine Measurement ; l'un comme l'autre convient.

## Notes de mapping

- Mapper ici un poids cible calculé — **pas** un poids mesuré (le poids mesuré relève du jeu *Body weight*).
- **Le poids idéal ajusté est une autre grandeur** : *1073500 / 1304200008 — Adjusted ideal body weight (SNOMED)* est calculé à partir de l'IBW et du poids réel (corrigé de l'obésité). Il a la même unité mais diffère de l'IBW dès que le poids réel en diffère, nettement chez le patient obèse : il ne fait donc pas partie de ce set, car le mélanger fausserait un volume courant exprimé par kg d'IBW.

reviews.comments:
## Summary
**Needs revision** Why are multiple concepts available for ideal body weight? Should be a single one, otherwise it's not clear which one to use?

## Use in our quality indicators
- Used in QI01 (Lung-protective ventilation in ARDS), QI03 (Feeding).
- CQL: 1 of 3 concepts are referenced in [`IndicateQiElements.cql`](https://github.com/umg-minai/cql-indicate-qi/blob/d63eb84a308d5586fcede0b7e3fa73abf6b6761c/cql/IndicateQiElements.cql?plain=1): [4062985](https://github.com/umg-minai/cql-indicate-qi/blob/d63eb84a308d5586fcede0b7e3fa73abf6b6761c/cql/IndicateQiElements.cql?plain=1#L36) (each ID links to its code definition).
- Not used by our indicators and not reviewed individually (2): 1073500 Adjusted ideal body weight, 3032445 Ideal body weight.

## Suggestions
- Remove all but the LOINC or the SNOMED concept

reviews.comments:
**Reply to the review of Gregor Lichtner**

Agreed: v1.2.0 removes **1073500** *Adjusted ideal body weight*. It has the same unit (kg) but is a different quantity: derived from IBW and actual body weight, it differs from IBW whenever the actual weight does, markedly in obese patients, and would bias a tidal volume per kg of IBW. It would need its own concept set.

Needs discussion:
- **Keep both 4062985** *Ideal body weight* (SNOMED) **and 3032445** *Ideal body weight* (LOINC)? They are exactly the same concept, both standard and in the Measurement domain, so either one is correct for a data provider. A concept set gathers all the standard concepts of one variable, so that every site is captured whichever vocabulary it mapped to.

What do you think?
